chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Concerning a man who struck another man on his head, and his tongue became impaired: the letters of the alphabet are to be presented to him in full, then he is to be given the diyah in proportion to what he is unable to articulate from them.

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: financial compensation due for bodily injury
key_terms.بِحِصَّةِ: in proportion to or according to the share of
key_terms.ثَقُلَ: became impaired or heavy, meaning speech was made difficult
key_terms.حُرُوفُ: letters, used as the basis for testing articulation
key_terms.لِسَانُهُ: his tongue, referring here to his faculty of speech

ai.seo_question: How is diyah calculated in Shi'i fiqh for someone whose speech is impaired after being struck on the head?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for assessing compensation when a head injury causes impairment in speech. The injured person is tested against all the letters of the alphabet, and diyah is awarded according to the proportion of letters he can no longer pronounce properly.
